context: Daichi's family home in Osaka. His mother (Sachiko, playing the part of his elderly mom in this scene) has been waiting all afternoon for him to drop in.
purpose: adult-son visit home — affectionate maternal interrogation, soft underneath

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.style: Bright, loud Kansai-tinged joy. Already rising from her seat in the voice. Opening attack delighted and welcoming.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: ごめん、母さん、本当に。仕事、長くて。
lines.en: Sorry, Mom — really. Work went long.
lines.style: Genuine apology, shoulders still carrying the weight of the day. Bag still on his shoulder in the delivery. Apologetic but not self-pitying.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: ええの、ええの。座って、座って。ご飯あるで。
lines.en: It's fine, it's fine. Sit down, sit down. There's food.
lines.style: Three warm commands stacked like a ritual. Matter-of-fact hospitality. The tone of someone who's said this a thousand times and means it every time.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.style: The bag drops in the voice — real attention now. Warm and genuinely interested. The shift from apology to presence.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 元気、元気。あんたは？最近、本当に痩せた気がする。
lines.en: Just fine, just fine. What about you? Honestly, you look thinner lately.
lines.style: A diagnostic mother-look carried in the words. Matter-of-fact observation mixed with concern. Slight narrowing of attention.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.style: Reflexive deflection with a small smile underneath. Quick, light pushback. The automatic son-response to mother-worry.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うそや。お母さんの目、本当に騙されへんで。
lines.en: You're lying. A mother's eyes — really, they don't miss anything.
lines.style: Slides a plate across the table in the delivery. The diagnostic eye narrowed with gentle certainty. Warm but unmoved by his denial.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.style: A genuine Kansai laugh, real and unforced. Half-surrender in the voice, hands up in the rhythm of it. Warmth and acceptance.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: ちゃんと食べんと、大変なことになるで。
lines.en: You've got to eat properly, or you'll run yourself into the ground.
lines.style: A small mother-warning, delivered with half-real, half-playful weight. The caring underneath the directive. Slight edge of actual concern.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: はい、はい。…でも、本当に、母さんの料理、いちばん。
lines.en: Yes, yes. …But really — your cooking is the best.
lines.style: A small unguarded compliment. The words come simple and true, not performed. Genuine throughout — quiet sincerity.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: (small laugh) お世辞、上手なって。
lines.en: (small laugh) You've learned how to flatter me so well.
lines.style: A small pleased laugh. Warm and knowing. Pours tea in the rhythm of the words. Not fooled but delighted by the attempt.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.style: A small, firm correction. Mouth full perhaps, but the words come clear and steady. Insistent on the truth of it.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 一人で、ちゃんと食べてる？
lines.en: Are you eating properly on your own?
lines.style: The real question beneath the previous lines. Quieter, more direct. The concern finally asked outright. Steady and waiting for honesty.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: …まあ、ちゃんと、とは言えへんかも。
lines.en: …Well — properly might be too strong a word.
lines.style: A small, honest concession. The voice quieter, defenses down. A small admission of struggle, delivered without drama.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 本当のこと、ありがとう。ちゃんとしぃや、時間あるから今日は。
lines.en: Thank you for being honest with me. Take care of yourself — we've got time together today.
lines.style: Real warmth and acceptance. The whole afternoon is offered in the delivery. Gentle, patient, and present.
